Nina Park: Aurora HW team asked for a fast perf-vs-watt validation next week. They want a single artifact pack: raw curves, a pass/fail sheet for marketplace, and kernel tuning notes. Who owns what?

Diego Ruiz: I can own the curves and CSV format. Propose minimal fields: run_id, model, seq, batch, idle_w, avg_w, peak_w, tok_s, p50_ms, kernel_tag, notes.

Tom Yates: I'll handle kernel tweaks and safe defaults. Note: Aurora images are locked so we must supply a signed livepatch or a user-space shim.

bench-bot: aurora-watt-pp run scheduled  start=2026-05-05T07:00Z duration=24h runners=4 owner=@Nina Park

Nina Park: Diego, drop a CSV example here and a one-line repro for CI.

Diego Ruiz: CSV sample: run_id,model,seq,batch,idle_w,avg_w,peak_w,tok_s,p50_ms,kernel_tag,notes
or-20260505-1,redwood-3b,2048,1,78.4,402.1,448.7,820.5,13.2,aurora-5.15-live,firstpass

Repro (CI): docker run --rm --gpus all redwood/bench:stable --model redwood-3b --seq 2048 --batch 1 --profile power --out /tmp/$RUN.csv

Tom Yates: Checklist: 1) confirm PMIC mapping from partner; 2) pin cpus, set governor=performance; 3) disable c-states; 4) apply livepatch SHA and run 3 warmup passes; 5) capture per-socket energy counters. I'll add rollback script if livepatch fails.

Nina Park: Acceptance: marketplace pass if perf/W >= +6% vs baseline, thermal <78C sustained, and throughput stddev <3% across 3 runs.

Tom Yates: Risk (1-liner): livepatch blocked -> fallback to shim + longer validation.

Diego Ruiz: Risk: power sensor mismatch -> mitigation: record idle baseline and upload calibration file with each run.

Nina Park: I'll send a short kickoff invite to Aurora infra for Tue 9am PT. Drop comments here for traceability.
